fullDescription.text: Unauthorized privilege escalation on AppServer due to misconfiguration or vulnerability
Data corruption or tampering in DatabaseServer via unauthorized write access
Unauthorized access to sensitive data stored in DatabaseServer leading to data breach

shortDescription.text: [HIGH] Elevation of Privilege — Client Web Browser

fullDescription.text: Unauthorized privilege escalation on Client Web Browser due to misconfiguration or vulnerability
Critical Elevation of Privilege: Unauthenticated data flow from AppServer is allowed to interact with a critical database DatabaseServer.
Unpatched OS or software vulnerabilities on AppServer leading to system compromise
Unpatched OS or software vulnerabilities on Client Web Browser leading to system compromise
Data interception on an unencrypted channel from Load Balancer to WebServer (Man-in-the-Middle attack)
Data interception on an unencrypted channel from WebServer to AppServer (Man-in-the-Middle attack)
Data interception on an unencrypted channel from AppServer to DatabaseServer (Man-in-the-Middle attack)
Data interception on an unencrypted channel from DatabaseServer to AppServer (Man-in-the-Middle attack)
Privilege abuse by actor End User to gain unauthorized access or perform unauthorized actions
Application-layer flood (HTTP requests or slow connections) exhausting web server WebServer
Potential for spoofing attacks on data crossing trust boundaries from WebServer to AppServer without proper authentication
Denial of Service against DatabaseServer through resource-intensive queries or excessive connections
Insecure security configuration or hardening on AppServer leading to information exposure
Lack of monitoring or logging on AppServer, preventing detection of malicious activities and enabling repudiation
Insecure security configuration or hardening on Client Web Browser leading to information exposure
Weak SSL/TLS configuration or ciphers used by Load Balancer leading to information disclosure
Volumetric network flood saturating load balancer Load Balancer and every service behind it
No audit trail of data changes in DatabaseServer, so modifications cannot be attributed to a user
Session hijacking or fixation attack against the Load Balancer leading to unauthorized access
Spoofing of data from End User to Load Balancer due to lack of authentication
Spoofing of data from Load Balancer to WebServer due to lack of authentication
Spoofing of data from WebServer to AppServer due to lack of authentication
Spoofing of data from AppServer to DatabaseServer due to lack of authentication
Spoofing of data from DatabaseServer to AppServer due to lack of authentication
Identity spoofing of the actor End User via phishing or credential theft
Lack of monitoring or logging on Client Web Browser, preventing detection of malicious activities and enabling repudiation
Repudiation of critical actions performed by End User due to insufficient logging or non-repudiation controls
